newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Bid to lift S.African central bank secrecy veil.
newsitem.headline: Bid to lift S.African central bank secrecy veil.

text.p: The parliamentary finance committee on Tuesday broadened the scope of a draft bill intended to limit the veil of secrecy that surrounds the South African Reserve Bank's relations with client banks.

Despite objections from opposition parties, the African National Congress-dominated committee recast the proposed Reserve Bank Amendment Bill to allow for disclosure of a wide range of relations between the central bank and client banks.
The committee forced a change to the proposed bill, removing the effective veto of commercial banks on the disclosure of information involving them.

The version of the bill approved by the committee on Tuesday gives the Minister of Finance and the Governor of the Reserve Bank the right to publish certain classes of information about client banks without their approval.
The bill was prompted by objections to the secrecy surrounding so-called "lifeboat operations" in which the central bank has rescued commercial banks from insolvency or collapse.
In terms of current legislation, these operations can be disclosed only if the rescued institution gives permission.

If the bill approved by the committee on Tuesday is passed by parliament, the Reserve Bank and the Finance Ministry will be obliged only to consult the client bank about disclosure and not to honour their preference for secrecy.
